_comment: Venues whose LISTING page carries their calendar as schema.org markup,
so the whole roster costs one request. Discovered by jsonld.py from the
census's `jsonld_event` signal, which is narrower than `jsonld_detail`:
54% of sites carry JSON-LD and 7% carry an Event, and the difference is
Organization/WebSite boilerplate that describes the site rather than
REPLACED each run except for hand-set `skip`, `why` and `venue_name`.
An events count is a fact about today; a skip is a judgement about the
site and must not be undone by a re-probe.
`locations` is every distinct location.name seen, and it is the field to
read before trusting a site: a venue calendar names its own rooms, while
an aggregator names other people's. Events carry a PostalAddress and no
coordinates, so each location is geocoded from its street address rather
than inheriting one point per host -- which is what lets a club with
three rooms place all three correctly.

venues.why: Not a venue calendar. Every event names another room -- Palace Theater, Beacon Theater -- and links to newyorkcitytheatre.com, so this is an aggregator republishing other people's listings under a theatre's domain. Good markup is not evidence that a page is about the site serving it.

venues.name: ChaShaMa
venues.why: Crawled 52 event pages and not one carries an Event object -- the census saw the markup on a different page shape than /event/<id> serves. 52 requests a run for nothing is exactly what the politeness in lib/http exists to prevent. Re-check if the site is rebuilt.

venues.name: The PIT
venues.why: Backed off. The host answered 93 links and 60 page reads at one second apart, then stopped answering anything at all -- /events and /robots.txt both time out. That our crawl caused it is not proven and the timing is exactly what a rate-limit block looks like, so the honest response is to stop asking rather than to retry on a schedule. It was the best detail-mode venue here, 17 live events, and it is worth re-enabling by hand once it answers again -- with a lower cap than the one that may have done this.
